blueprint.system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

correction_history.issue: Initial lead-in said pathogenic variants causing LHON generally impair one respiratory-chain complex. GeneReviews documents rare LHON-associated variants in MT-CYB, MT-CO3 and MT-ATP6 as well as MT-ND genes, so the universal wording was overbroad.
correction_history.correction: Lead-in narrowed to the most common pathogenic variants.
correction_history.evidence: GeneReviews reports the three common mtDNA variants in MT-ND1, MT-ND4 and MT-ND6 account for approximately 90% of LHON and encode complex-I subunits.

claim_audit.phenotype: MedlinePlus and GeneReviews support young-adult onset, painless subacute central visual loss that may start in one eye and involve the other within weeks/months; GeneReviews supports central/centrocecal scotomas.
claim_audit.inheritance: MedlinePlus and GeneReviews directly support mitochondrial/maternal inheritance; an unaffected mother can carry the mtDNA variant and affected maternal relatives are compatible with reduced penetrance.
claim_audit.common_variants: GeneReviews identifies m.3460G>A in MT-ND1, m.11778G>A in MT-ND4 and m.14484T>C in MT-ND6 as the three common variants accounting for about 90% of LHON.
claim_audit.correct_complex: MedlinePlus mitochondrial-DNA page identifies MT-ND1, MT-ND4, MT-ND4L and MT-ND6 LHON genes as encoding complex-I proteins; GeneReviews describes complex-I respiratory-chain dysfunction.
claim_audit.distractor_1: NCBI electron-transport-chain review identifies complex II as succinate dehydrogenase transferring electrons from succinate/FADH2 to ubiquinone, distinct from MT-ND complex-I proteins.
claim_audit.distractor_2: NCBI electron-transport-chain review identifies complex III as the cytochrome bc1 complex transferring electrons from ubiquinol to cytochrome c; the common LHON MT-ND genes are not complex-III subunits.
claim_audit.distractor_3: NCBI electron-transport-chain review identifies complex IV as cytochrome c oxidase transferring electrons to oxygen; the common LHON variants named above affect complex I instead.
claim_audit.distractor_4: NCBI electron-transport-chain review identifies complex V as ATP synthase using the proton gradient to synthesize ATP; it is not the complex encoded by the common LHON MT-ND genes.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Sequential painless bilateral central optic neuropathy in a young man plus affected maternal-line relatives strongly identifies LHON. The question then asks specifically about the most common pathogenic variants, which GeneReviews localizes to MT-ND1/ND4/ND6, all complex-I genes.
adversarial_second_pass.rare_variant_challenge: Rare LHON-associated variants exist in genes encoding complexes III, IV and V. This would have made the original universal lead-in ambiguous; after narrowing to 'most common pathogenic variants,' complex I is uniquely correct.
adversarial_second_pass.maternal_unaffected_challenge: An unaffected mother does not weaken the diagnosis because penetrance is incomplete and women carrying LHON mtDNA variants may remain asymptomatic.
adversarial_second_pass.sequential_eye_challenge: MedlinePlus explicitly supports one eye being affected first and the fellow eye becoming involved weeks to months later.
adversarial_second_pass.complex_ii_challenge: Complex II is nuclear-encoded succinate dehydrogenase and not the respiratory-chain target of the common LHON MT-ND variants.
adversarial_second_pass.option_parallelism: All options are respiratory-chain complexes I-V with equivalent grammatical form, eliminating category or length cueing.
adversarial_second_pass.hidden_assumption_check: No prevalence estimate, treatment rule, threshold, dose or unprovided genetic-test result is required to select the answer.
